title: Characterization of the raw path encoding
statement: Let $x$ and $M$ be finite Boolean words and let $n,s,t$ be natural numbers. Then $x$ is the encoding of the pair consisting of $n$ true bits and the nested pair of $M$ with the pair of the binary expansions of $s$ and $t$ (using the encoding that doubles each bit of the first component, appends $01$, and then appends the second component) if and only if all of the following hold: starting at position $0$, the first $n$ bits are each doubled and followed by the separator $01$; starting at position $2n+2$, the bits of $M$ are each doubled and followed by $01$; starting at position $2n+2+2|M|+2$, the bits of the binary expansion of $s$ are each doubled and followed by $01$; and starting at position $2n+2+2|M|+2+2|	ext{binary expansion of }s|+2$, the binary expansion of $t$ appears verbatim and ends exactly at the end of $x$. In each doubled segment, both copies of every bit agree with the corresponding bit of that segment's word; positions beyond the end of $x$ are interpreted as false when checking these conditions.
